heading: Build valid parens incrementally
body:
Don't enumerate all strings and filter — **build only valid ones** by tracking open/close counts.

**Two pruning rules:**
- Add `(` only if `open < n`
- Add `)` only if `close < open`

When `len(s) == 2*n`, you've got a valid combo.

heading: Why close < open matters
body:
Adding `)` when `close >= open` creates an **unmatched closing bracket** — the string breaks immediately.

Example: `)(` is invalid from the start. You need an opening `(` before every closing `)`.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why can we only add a closing parenthesis ')' when close < open?
options: To ensure we don't exceed n pairs of parentheses
To prevent creating an invalid string with unmatched closing parentheses
To optimize the time complexity of the algorithm
To avoid duplicate combinations in the result
explain: Adding ')' when close >= open would create an invalid string where a closing parenthesis appears without a matching opening parenthesis before it.
